As someone who is deeply fascinated with systematics, I am wholly disheartened when people continue to argue that there is no concrete evidence for evolution, when the description of evolution is the process of change over time.

Speciation doesn't have a catalyst, it is a phenomena that happens gradually as two individuals of a species become independent of each other genetically, to the point that the two cannot interact anymore, either due to population separation, environmental stress, mutation, and/or adaptation.

"Missing Links" are not these random in between forms that explain "ah, so that is where this came from!" Missing links give us an understanding of change, they show how something diverged, not proof of what it came from because what it is, but an ancestral form for other things to develop from, not develop into. Nothing "turns" into something else, every form exists for a period, and at some point the divergent partner exists at the same time as the ancestor, there is no exception to this, because the ancestor is still trying to be viable, still trying to do nothing but survive.

Devolution is also not real, as evolution is effected by multiple variables, such as population size and its range of spread, not just fitness. And fitness only means a species ability to adapt to its environment, not its superiority to other life forms. Evolution does not work towards improvement, it works toward stability. In reality, evolution settles for "good enough" when it comes to coping with an environmental stressor.

Even the statement, "more evolved" is misplaced. To be "more evolved" means having gone through more change over time, which means having survived longer and still been viable even after extinction events, so in reality humans have not evolved much at all compared to older life forms like velvet worms, crinoids, and mollusks that have been around since the Cambrian Era, the Era that marks the start of complex life on earth.

Evolution isn't concrete because evolution is broad, it happens everywhere, to everyone and everything, everyday, at a variable rate just fast enough that you can notice it, but not until at least a sizable amount of time has passed, and most importantly, effects everything differently.

It is a theory because it own definition undergoes its own processes as we discover more information. Theories can change because they should be changed to fit the right information. However, thinking differently does not subjugate an idea to be held to the same respect as the established premise, and should always be held to a scrutiny that truly tests its viability.

Finally, do not believe the first step to discovery is to try and debunk or prove something. That is true failure as a scientist, as biasing yourself will only make you find what you want,and not find the truth.
